![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/2f0c94bc3100b4fd9754ee822f55e2edbae8475bece3b18ac34f63e6c92267a2.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
